jobs.title: Director, Architecture
jobs.description:
Job Description

You will be working on a flexible hybrid schedule as part of Fidelity’s dynamic working arrangement.

The work location for this role is 483 Bay Street in Toronto until approximately late 2026, when the work location will change to the new Mississauga office at 3 Robert Speck Parkway.

Current work authorization for Canada is required for all openings.

At Fidelity, we’ve been helping Canadian investors build better financial futures for over 35 years. We offer individuals and institutions a range of trusted investment portfolios and services - and we’re constantly seeking to find new and better ways to help our clients. As a privately owned company, we boldly embrace innovation in all areas as we continue to grow our business into the future.

Working with us means you’ll be part of a diverse and dedicated group of people who make a real difference for our clients and communities every day. You’ll have a wide range of opportunities to grow and develop your career in an inclusive environment where you’ll feel valued and supported to be your best - both personally and professionally.

How You’ll Make An Impact

The Director, Architecture & Technology Strategy reports to the Vice President, AI and is responsible for shaping and executing the enterprise architecture and technology strategy for Fidelity Investments Canada. The role provides strategic and people leadership across enterprise, domain, solution and data architecture, ensuring these capabilities evolve in support of the firm's business priorities, technology modernization and AI ambitions.

The successful candidate will combine strong strategic thinking, technical depth and business partnership skills. They will work closely with senior business and technology leaders to translate enterprise priorities into target-state architecture, technology capabilities, standards and multi-year roadmaps that support long-term growth, operational resilience and transformation.

A critical part of the role is close partnership with Fidelity International (FIL). The Director will maintain visibility into evolving FIL strategies, standards, platforms and capabilities and work collaboratively with international partners to shape a joint Canada-FIL roadmap, identifying where Canada should adopt, extend, contribute to or influence enterprise capabilities.

The Director leads and develops the Architecture teams, strengthening the maturity of the function, its operating model, governance practices and technical capabilities. They work closely with Business, AI, Engineering, Security, Risk and Governance partners on key strategic initiatives, ensuring enterprise architecture supports modern engineering practices, technology modernization and the adoption of advanced analytics, generative AI and agentic AI while maintaining appropriate security, resilience and control.

Translates long-term business objectives into target-state architecture, technology capabilities, standards and investment priorities and establishes a clear multi-year technology roadmap.
Defines and maintains enterprise architecture direction across business, application, integration, data, cloud and technology domains, ensuring alignment between business strategy and technology decisions.
Shapes enterprise technology strategy, providing strategic guidance on technology investments, platform selection, modernization opportunities and emerging technologies while balancing innovation, resilience, security and cost efficiency.
Establishes and continuously matures architecture governance, principles, reference architectures and decision-making practices to enable consistent, pragmatic and effective technology decisions.
Partners with Engineering and Technology leaders to identify and prioritize technology modernization, technical debt reduction, technology lifecycle management and architectural simplification.
Ensures AI and emerging technology requirements are incorporated into enterprise architecture, data architecture, integration patterns and platform strategy, supporting the adoption of generative AI, agentic AI and AI-enabled software development.
Leads, develops and matures the Architecture function, establishing clear accountabilities, operating practices and decision rights across enterprise, domain, solution and data architecture teams.
Hires, coaches, mentors and develops leaders and technical talent and establishes clear goals, development plans and performance expectations.
Builds a culture of strong technical leadership, collaboration, accountability, continuous learning and constructive challenge.

What We’re Looking For

University degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, Data, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
10+ years of progressive experience in technology, enterprise architecture or technology strategy, preferably in financial services or another complex regulated environment.
At least 5 years of people leadership experience managing technical subject matter experts and people managers.
Demonstrated experience defining and executing enterprise architecture and technology strategies, leading multidisciplinary technical teams and partnering with senior business and technology leaders on major transformation and modernization initiatives.
Experience building and maturing architecture capabilities, establishing architecture standards, governance practices and technology roadmaps in complex organizations.
Experience working in a global organization and developing enterprise architecture or technology capabilities across regions; financial services experience strongly preferred.
Relevant enterprise architecture, cloud or data management certification such as TOGAF, AWS, Snowflake or CDMP.

The Skills Set You Bring

Deep understanding of enterprise architecture and technology strategy, with the ability to connect business strategy to technology capabilities, architectural direction and investment decisions.
Strong knowledge of modern cloud and data platforms, including Snowflake and AWS, and the architecture patterns required for scalable, secure enterprise technology capabilities.
Strong knowledge of enterprise, domain, solution and data architecture, including application design, integration patterns, data modelling, semantic layers and enterprise information architecture.
Strong understanding of technology modernization, architecture governance, technical debt management, technology lifecycle management and enterprise architecture standards.
Broad knowledge of enterprise architecture across applications, integration, cloud, security and technology domains and experience establishing target-state architecture and multi-year technology roadmaps.
Strong understanding of how enterprise architecture and modern engineering practices enable AI, machine learning, generative AI, agentic AI and AI-enabled software development at enterprise scale.
Demonstrated ability to build and mature architecture practices, develop technical talent and establish effective operating models and decision-making frameworks.
Exceptional leadership, interpersonal, communication, presentation and relationship-management skills, including the ability to influence senior business, technology and international stakeholders.
Strong strategic judgement, analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate emerging technologies, balance short-term delivery with long-term direction and lead through ambiguity

Some of the ways we’ll help you feel valued and supported as part of our team

Flexible working arrangements that vary based on role requirements
Competitive total compensation, including company contributions to your group RRSP without a matching requirement from you
Comprehensive health benefits that start on your first day, with 100% employer-paid premiums, that include up to $6000 annually for mental health services and therapy
Parental leave top-up to 100% of your salary for a period of 25 weeks
Up to $650 for home office equipment
Generous time off policy, including 2 paid days annually to volunteer at a charity of your choice
Diversity and inclusion programs, including an active network of Employee Resource Groups
Extensive professional development opportunities, including access to over 11,000 training and development courses, tuition reimbursement, and monetary rewards for completing a required designation

We care a lot about fostering a compassionate, people-centric culture, and are proud to have been named one of Canada’s Top 100 employers for the last five years.

BC Transit is entering an important phase of technology modernization. As artificial intelligence, automation, Internet of Things (IoT), SmartBus technology and digital services continue to reshape public transit, the organization is strengthening its core systems and simplifying processes. jobs.title: Finance Director, Canada
jobs.description:
What this job involves:

We are seeking an exceptional, strategic finance leader to serve as Finance Director for our Canada team, overseeing a business generating $250+ million in revenue across Real Estate Management Services, Markets, and Leasing. This is a high-impact, business-partnering role for a finance professional who thrives on influencing strategy rather than simply reporting on it — someone who can surface the right data at the right moment, challenge assumptions constructively, and serve as a trusted sounding board to senior business leaders across the region. You'll drive financial planning and reporting while shaping the corporate strategy and vision for Canada, working hand-in-hand with leadership to translate financial insight into decisive action. The ideal candidate understands commercial real estate and professional services, exceptional partnering skills, and high level corporate finance.

This role is based out of JLL's Corporate office in Toronto and requires being in-office 4 days/week (flexibility to work remote one day/week). The Finance Director leads a small team and plays a key role on JLL Canada's Executive Leadership team. You will work closely with leaders across all business lines and report into a Global Finance team.

What your day-to-day will look like
:

Strategic Financial Leadership

Serve as the primary strategic finance partner and advisor to the Country CEO, country business line leaders, country functional leaders, and regional/global finance leadership.
Lead the preparation, management, consolidation, and delivery of the annual financial plan, reforecasts, and long-range planning efforts.
Drive proactive, data-informed decision-making across all stakeholder groups.
Translate global business line strategy into local Canada priorities, providing the financial insights and analysis that connect country-level execution to business line direction and identify opportunities to support revenue growth and margin improvement.
Oversee the integrity of all financial processes within your scope of responsibility.
Bridge discussions between business leadership and technical finance teams to inform, guide and influence business decisions

Performance Management & Reporting

Lead the preparation and delivery of comprehensive monthly financial reporting and analysis for country, business, and finance leadership.
Produce and analyze monthly/quarterly financial variance reports with actionable insights.
Develop pipeline reporting and key performance metrics for business and service lines.
Facilitate pipeline reviews as a forum to inform decision-making and develop forecasts.
Oversee all fiscal reporting activities, ensuring timeliness, accuracy, and strategic relevance.
Own the month-end close cadence in partnership with the Controllership team, ensuring timely and accurate financial close.
Identify and diagnose the root cause(s) of margin variance and proactively bring recommendations to remedy

Client & Commercial Finance

Lead finance input on major client relationships and contracts, including pricing, fee structuring & negotiations, and contract issue resolution.
Support client-specific commercial finance matters such as capital-funded project reimbursements and rebate pool administration, in partnership with account and operations teams.

Leadership & Team Development

Lead and develop a high-performing finance team within the realm of FP&A and business partnering.
Create and execute succession planning and professional development programs.
Partner in compensation planning and design to ensure alignment with organizational objectives.
Foster a culture of excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Act as an ambassador for the broader Finance function across the organization

Required qualiﬁcations:

10+ years progressive financial leadership experience.
Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Finance, Accounting, or Commerce.
Proven track record of leading financial strategy and operations in complex businesses.
Outstanding business partnership skills with experience advising and shaping strategy alongside business unit executives.
Experience leading high-performing teams through periods of growth and change.
Superior analytical capabilities and financial modelling expertise
Exceptional communication skills with the ability to translate complex financial concepts.
Strategic mindset with demonstrated ability to drive business results.
Demonstrated experience owning a planning/budgeting cycle forecast process for a business unit or country.

Preferred qualiﬁcations:

CPA/CFA preferred.
Bilingual English/French considered a strong asset.

jobs.title: Director, I&IT Data Platform & Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Description

Metrolinx is connecting communities across the Greater Golden Horseshoe. Metrolinx operates GO Transit and UP Express, as well as the PRESTO fare payment system. We are also building new and improved rapid transit, including GO Expansion, Light Rail Transit routes, and major expansions to Toronto’s subway system, to get people where they need to go, better, faster and easier. Metrolinx is an agency of the Government of Ontario.

At Metrolinx, equity, diversity and inclusion are essential to living our values of serving with passion, thinking forward and playing as a team.

Metrolinx's Innovation and Information Technology group supports female team members via "Go Tech Women" an affinity group for women in Information Technology, led by our Chief Information Officer.

If you enjoy technology and innovation, value diversity, appreciate work/balance and are looking for an opportunity to make a better world via public service, Metrolinx would like to hear from you!

Reporting to the VP, I&IT Enterprise AI & Data Centre of Excellence, the Director, Enterprise Data Platform & Engineering is accountable for the strategy, engineering, delivery and operation of Metrolinx's enterprise data platform and the trusted data foundation that enables analytics, artificial intelligence and data-driven decision-making across the organization.

The Director leads the modernization and evolution of Metrolinx's enterprise data platform, including cloud data infrastructure, data lake/lakehouse capabilities, data engineering, integration, DataOps and platform services. The role is accountable for establishing scalable, secure and reusable platform capabilities based on a "build once, reuse many times" approach, enabling business units to access trusted data and deliver data and AI products more efficiently.

Working within a federated operating model where business areas retain accountability for their data and business outcomes, the Director partners with business leaders, I&IT, Enterprise Architecture, Data Governance, Cybersecurity, AI teams and strategic vendors to ensure enterprise data capabilities are secure, governed, interoperable, cost-effective and aligned with Metrolinx's Enterprise Data and AI strategies.

The Director also provides leadership to multidisciplinary engineering teams and strategic partners, establishing modern engineering practices, platform standards and delivery disciplines while building the organizational capabilities required to scale data and AI across Metrolinx.

What will I be doing?

Strategy and leadership: Develop and operationalize Metrolinx's Enterprise Data Platform strategy and roadmap, translating the Enterprise Data and AI strategies into platform capabilities, investment priorities and measurable maturity targets.
Platform ownership: Own the enterprise data platform as a strategic enterprise capability, including its architecture, engineering, scalability, performance, reliability, lifecycle and ongoing evolution.
Data platform modernization: Lead the modernization of Metrolinx's data environment toward a scalable, cloud-native and AI-ready architecture, evolving data lake and related capabilities into a modern enterprise data platform that supports analytics, reporting, machine learning, generative AI and enterprise data products.
Data engineering: Establish and lead enterprise data engineering capabilities, including ingestion, integration, transformation, orchestration and reusable data pipelines, enabling trusted data to move efficiently from source systems into enterprise analytical and AI environments.
Engineering excellence: Establish engineering standards and practices for DataOps, DevOps, CI/CD, Infrastructure-as-Code, automated testing, observability, monitoring and release management to improve the quality, speed and reliability of data platform delivery.
AI-ready data foundation: Partner with AI teams to ensure enterprise data and platform capabilities can securely support machine learning, advanced analytics and generative AI use cases, including appropriate data access, integration, scalability, governance and operational controls.
Reusable data capabilities: Establish common enterprise data services, patterns and reusable components that reduce duplication and accelerate the delivery of data, analytics and AI solutions across Metrolinx.
Delivery management: Deliver projects on scope, on time and on budget, using a Lean Agile approach with clear milestones. Work with Scrum Masters, Product Owners and vendors to prioritize software work and keep quality high.
Enterprise data architecture: Own and evolve Metrolinx's enterprise data architecture, including target-state architecture, standards, principles, patterns and roadmaps. Establish architectural guardrails for data platforms, integration, storage, data movement and data products to enable interoperability, reuse and scalability across the enterprise. Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Cybersecurity, Data Governance and business technology teams to ensure data solutions align with broader enterprise architecture and technology strategies.
Architecture governance: Establish and oversee data architecture governance to ensure new solutions and investments align with enterprise data standards and target-state architecture, reducing duplication, technical debt and unnecessary point-to-point integration.
Executive communication: Run strategic workshops with the business to define goals and requirements. Prepare regular updates for the CIO, CFO and executive team. Handle escalations with solutions ready.
Stakeholder partnerships: Build trusted relationships at executive and working levels with internal teams, vendors, partners, government and agencies. Act as a Metrolinx ambassador in public presentations and meetings.
Financial stewardship: Own annual and long-term budgets, staffing plans and ROI. Put in place the controls and reporting for cost management. Hold signing authority within the role's scope.
People leadership: Lead a large department through subordinate supervisors. Set clear roles and expectations, give timely feedback and address performance gaps. Build a "best company to work for" culture.
Talent and vendor scale-up: Work with other senior technology leaders to scale a 50+ member team of internal and external resources across multiple geographies. Keep the talent and vendor mix right. Mentor talent in line with future I&IT strategy.

What Skills and Qualifications Do I Need?

Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data/Information Management or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training and senior-level experience.
Significant leadership experience building and operating enterprise-scale data platforms, data engineering capabilities and cloud data environments within a complex organization.
Strong knowledge of modern data-platform architectures, including cloud data platforms, data lakes/lakehouses, data warehousing, data integration, APIs and distributed data-processing patterns.
Demonstrated experience modernizing legacy data environments and establishing cloud-native, scalable and reusable data-platform capabilities.
Strong understanding of Microsoft Azure data technologies and contemporary platforms such as Azure Databricks and Microsoft Fabric, or comparable enterprise technologies.
Experience establishing DataOps/DevOps practices, CI/CD, Infrastructure-as-Code, automated testing, observability and production engineering standards.
Demonstrated experience enabling enterprise analytics, machine learning and generative AI workloads through well-governed and scalable data platforms.
Strong knowledge of enterprise data governance, data quality, metadata, master/reference data, security, privacy and lifecycle management, and the ability to translate these requirements into platform capabilities.
Experience operating within a federated data model, enabling business-owned data products while maintaining enterprise standards, interoperability and governance.
Demonstrated experience leading large multidisciplinary teams and strategic vendors across onshore, offshore and/or nearshore delivery models.
Strong financial management experience, including cloud consumption management, technology investment planning, vendor management and platform FinOps.
Proven ability to translate complex technical issues into clear recommendations and communicate credibly with CIO/CFO/executive-level stakeholders.
Strong understanding of Agile product and platform delivery models and experience managing enterprise technology portfolios involving multiple business units and dependencies.

Don’t Meet Every Requirement?

If you’re excited about working with Metrolinx but your past experience doesn’t quite align with every qualification of this posting, we encourage you to apply. You just might be the right candidate for this or other roles. We are always looking for great talent to join our team.

We invite all interested individuals to apply and encourage applications from members of equity-deserving communities, including those who identify as Indigenous, Black, racialized, women, people with disabilities, and people with diverse gender identities, expressions and sexual orientations.

Accommodation

Metrolinx is an equal opportunity employer and committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce. We are also committed to offering reasonable accommodation to job applicants in accordance with applicable legislation. If you require assistance or an accommodation at any point during the hiring process, please contact us at: 416-202-5601 or email hr.recruitment@metrolinx.com.

Application Process

All applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada. Metrolinx will be using email to communicate with you for all job competitions. It is your responsibility to include an updated email address that is checked daily and accepts emails from unknown users. As we send time-sensitive correspondence, we recommend that you check your email regularly. If no response is received, we will assume you are no longer interested in pursuing the opportunity. Please be advised that a Criminal Record Check may be required of the successful candidate.

For Internal applicants, with the recent implementation of the Internal Mobility Policy, the internal recruitment process has changed for non-union roles. Candidates must be in their current role for 12 months prior to applying for another role and each applicant must be in good standing (not participating in a Performance Improvement Plan). Please review all provisions of the policy before submitting your application.

Should it be determined that any background information provided is misleading, inaccurate or incorrect, Metrolinx reserves the right to discontinue with the consideration of your application.

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

WE ARE AN EQUITABLE AND INCLUSIVE EMPLOYER.

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Ensures AI and emerging technology requirements are incorporated into enterprise architecture, data architecture, integration patterns and platform strategy, supporting the adoption of generative AI, agentic AI and AI-enabled software development.
Leads, develops and matures the Architecture function, establishing clear accountabilities, operating practices and decision rights across enterprise, domain, solution and data architecture teams.
Hires, coaches, mentors and develops leaders and technical talent and establishes clear goals, development plans and performance expectations.
Builds a culture of strong technical leadership, collaboration, accountability, continuous learning and constructive challenge.

What We’re Looking For

University degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, Data, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
10+ years of progressive experience in technology, enterprise architecture or technology strategy, preferably in financial services or another complex regulated environment.
At least 5 years of people leadership experience managing technical subject matter experts and people managers.
Demonstrated experience defining and executing enterprise architecture and technology strategies, leading multidisciplinary technical teams and partnering with senior business and technology leaders on major transformation and modernization initiatives.
Experience building and maturing architecture capabilities, establishing architecture standards, governance practices and technology roadmaps in complex organizations.
Experience working in a global organization and developing enterprise architecture or technology capabilities across regions; financial services experience strongly preferred.

The Skills Set You Bring

Deep understanding of enterprise architecture and technology strategy, with the ability to connect business strategy to technology capabilities, architectural direction and investment decisions.
Strong knowledge of modern cloud and data platforms, including Snowflake and AWS, and the architecture patterns required for scalable, secure enterprise technology capabilities.
Strong knowledge of enterprise, domain, solution and data architecture, including application design, integration patterns, data modelling, semantic layers and enterprise information architecture.
Strong understanding of technology modernization, architecture governance, technical debt management, technology lifecycle management and enterprise architecture standards.
Broad knowledge of enterprise architecture across applications, integration, cloud, security and technology domains and experience establishing target-state architecture and multi-year technology roadmaps.
Strong understanding of how enterprise architecture and modern engineering practices enable AI, machine learning, generative AI, agentic AI and AI-enabled software development at enterprise scale.
Demonstrated ability to build and mature architecture practices, develop technical talent and establish effective operating models and decision-making frameworks.
Exceptional leadership, interpersonal, communication, presentation and relationship-management skills, including the ability to influence senior business, technology and international stakeholders.
Strong strategic judgement, analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate emerging technologies, balance short-term delivery with long-term direction and lead through ambiguity

new_jobs.title: Finance Director, Canada
new_jobs.description:
What this job involves:

We are seeking an exceptional, strategic finance leader to serve as Finance Director for our Canada team, overseeing a business generating $250+ million in revenue across Real Estate Management Services, Markets, and Leasing. This is a high-impact, business-partnering role for a finance professional who thrives on influencing strategy rather than simply reporting on it — someone who can surface the right data at the right moment, challenge assumptions constructively, and serve as a trusted sounding board to senior business leaders across the region. You'll drive financial planning and reporting while shaping the corporate strategy and vision for Canada, working hand-in-hand with leadership to translate financial insight into decisive action. The ideal candidate understands commercial real estate and professional services, exceptional partnering skills, and high level corporate finance.

This role is based out of JLL's Corporate office in Toronto and requires being in-office 4 days/week (flexibility to work remote one day/week). The Finance Director leads a small team and plays a key role on JLL Canada's Executive Leadership team. You will work closely with leaders across all business lines and report into a Global Finance team.

What your day-to-day will look like
:

Strategic Financial Leadership

Serve as the primary strategic finance partner and advisor to the Country CEO, country business line leaders, country functional leaders, and regional/global finance leadership.
Lead the preparation, management, consolidation, and delivery of the annual financial plan, reforecasts, and long-range planning efforts.
Drive proactive, data-informed decision-making across all stakeholder groups.
Translate global business line strategy into local Canada priorities, providing the financial insights and analysis that connect country-level execution to business line direction and identify opportunities to support revenue growth and margin improvement.
Oversee the integrity of all financial processes within your scope of responsibility.
Bridge discussions between business leadership and technical finance teams to inform, guide and influence business decisions

Performance Management & Reporting

Lead the preparation and delivery of comprehensive monthly financial reporting and analysis for country, business, and finance leadership.
Produce and analyze monthly/quarterly financial variance reports with actionable insights.
Develop pipeline reporting and key performance metrics for business and service lines.
Facilitate pipeline reviews as a forum to inform decision-making and develop forecasts.
Oversee all fiscal reporting activities, ensuring timeliness, accuracy, and strategic relevance.
Own the month-end close cadence in partnership with the Controllership team, ensuring timely and accurate financial close.
Identify and diagnose the root cause(s) of margin variance and proactively bring recommendations to remedy

Client & Commercial Finance

Lead finance input on major client relationships and contracts, including pricing, fee structuring & negotiations, and contract issue resolution.
Support client-specific commercial finance matters such as capital-funded project reimbursements and rebate pool administration, in partnership with account and operations teams.

Leadership & Team Development

Lead and develop a high-performing finance team within the realm of FP&A and business partnering.
Create and execute succession planning and professional development programs.
Partner in compensation planning and design to ensure alignment with organizational objectives.
Foster a culture of excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Act as an ambassador for the broader Finance function across the organization

Required qualiﬁcations:

10+ years progressive financial leadership experience.
Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Finance, Accounting, or Commerce.
Proven track record of leading financial strategy and operations in complex businesses.
Outstanding business partnership skills with experience advising and shaping strategy alongside business unit executives.
Experience leading high-performing teams through periods of growth and change.
Superior analytical capabilities and financial modelling expertise
Exceptional communication skills with the ability to translate complex financial concepts.
Strategic mindset with demonstrated ability to drive business results.
Demonstrated experience owning a planning/budgeting cycle forecast process for a business unit or country.

Preferred qualiﬁcations:

CPA/CFA preferred.
Bilingual English/French considered a strong asset.
